items.evidence: leverage play <runs>/day-engine-8 --ticks 2: one JSON line, screen title, every brief key present (tick..records) with the no-season defaults.
--frame es_title.png --size 800x480 wrote a PNG; header reads 800 x 480; stall/day/settings/upgrades frames opened and viewed.
Fresh: texts Day Market, New season, Records, Stamps, Settings, Quit, menu_index 0; up at 0 stays 0, downs stop at 4; enter on Quit at tick 8 of --ticks 50 ended the run, printing tick 9 on title.

Settings start Language: English / Difficulty: Normal / Season: 7 days; left at English stays, right -> Espanol; difficulty easy..hard clamps; season 7<->3 clamps; Escape (tick 9) and Enter on Back both reached title.
Run with --settings A set es/hard; next run on A started es/hard/7; B set easy/3 -> next run easy/3. Fresh place: en/normal/7, slots [null,null,null], stamps [], records [].

Spanish run printed records, stamps, slots, morning, paused, stall, day, evening, upgrades (with No hay monedas suficientes), season over (Bancarrota) and title all in Spanish; settings texts switched to Ajustes/Idioma: Espanol the tick Right was given; es.json has the same 94 keys as en.json.
modules/work/strings/en.json and es.json hold the strings; README 'Adding a language' says how.
Fresh New season: texts New season, Slot 1: Empty, Slot 2: Empty, Slot 3: Empty; Escape -> title.
Enter on slot 2: screen morning, day 1, slot 2, coins 50, rep 50, all stock [], prices 4/6/11/14/7/9, upgrades [], crate_limit 8, order null, texts Morning, Day 1 of 7, Coins: 50.
Easy -> Coins: 60; Hard (Spanish run) -> Monedas: 40; easy/3: Day 1 of 3, forecast of 3; after pause->Title, settings changed to normal/7, Continue kept season_difficulty easy, season_length 3.
Seeds 1-7: forecasts of 7 entries among sun/cloud/heat/rain, weather = forecast[0], Weather: text follows (Cloud/Sun/Heat seen); same seed gave the same forecast across runs.
Seeds 1-7 and later days: all wholesale prices within base-1..base+2; rows like 'Apples: 4 a unit, stock 0', stock follows after buying.
Seed 1: Enter on Apples (4) coins 50->26, apples [{units 6, days_left 5}]; second lot -> 12 units in one batch, coins 2, row 'stock 12'; honey batch days_left null.

Not enough coins: coins 2, Enter on fish changed nothing and showed 'Not enough coins' until the next word (up). The 99-unit cap was never reached in play (needs over 96 units of one good), so not seen.
Day 1 order null; day 2 seed 1 'Order: 6 Apples for 36' (6*4*3/2), accept -> taken true, 'Order taken: 6 Apples for 36'; second accept changed nothing. Seed 3 day 2 '6 Cheese for 99'.
Later run on place D: title New season, Continue, Records...; Continue row 'Slot 1: Day 2 of 7, 50 coins'; after a fresh start slot row read Day 1 of 7, 50 coins in slots.
Continue with --seed 9 on saved day 2: same coins 50, rep 59, stall, prices, forecast, wholesale 1/2/5/7/4/4 and order 6 apples 36 as the unbroken run; Enter on empty Slot 2 changed nothing.

Escape on morning/stall/day -> Paused, Resume, Title; escape and Resume went back with same state; day paused ticks 201-400 clock stayed 8; Title after buying apples (coins 44) left slot at 50 coins, and Continue showed coins 50, stock empty.
Stall opens cursor (0,0), apples, texts Stall, Day 1 of 7, Good: Apples, Price: 4, Stock: 6, Crates: 0 of 8, Enter: open.
Down/Left at (0,0) stayed; Up -> (0,1), second Up stayed; Right x6 stopped at x 5.
prev_good from apples -> honey -> flowers; next_good cycles flowers, honey, apples, bread, cheese, fish; Good/Price/Stock texts follow.
put added crates and 'Crates: N of 8'; put on occupied cell (fish at 2,1) did nothing; 9 puts gave 8 crates; take removed, take on empty cell did nothing.
Apples price_up x10 stopped at 12, price_down x12 stopped at 1, Price text followed.
Apples price 5 and crate kept into day 2 stall; later run Continue on that place: prices apples 5, stall [(0,0) apples].
Enter on Stall: screen day, clock 0, speed slow, 08:00, Speed: Slow, taken/served/walked_out/passed 0, visitors list filled.
Script over 6 days' lists: ids 1..n, minutes strictly increasing in 0..479, types valid, wants distinct with counts 2/1/2/3; identical runs gave identical lists; other seeds different lists.
Slow: clock 93 after 1871 ticks; fast switch at progress 30 -> clock 1 three ticks later then every 5; rush +1 per tick; hold kept 08:12 while tick ran; Speed text followed.
finish at the first day tick gave evening, clock 480, and state md5 identical to the same day at rush/slow/fast.
Seed 1 day: slow, fast, rush, finish and a mix (fast, hold, rush, slow, fast, rush) gave identical md5 of coins, taken, served, walked_out, passed, sales, stock, rep.
Rush minute-by-minute: v1 (minute 7) x 0 at 7, x 2 at 9, off aisle and at till at 13; script checked x = clock - m and leaving at m+6 over ~2400 minutes, no errors.
Script over days without Sign: every take was a wanted, new good from the front crate of its column, or back crate after something in basket; no violations.
Apples at (2,0): cook v21 (m 136) held 2 apples at 4 at clock 138, budget 32; at price 5 the cook took none; tourist v1 took 1 at 6, none at 7.
Script checked budget_left = budget - spent, units*price within budget, and basket units on aisle+queue <= stock every minute: no errors.
Empty-basket visitors left the aisle and passed grew; queued visitors had joined = minute + 6 in every state checked.
v21 at till from 142 with 1 good: ends 145; script checked ends = s+2+n, bargain paid total - total/10, coins and taken rose by paid, sale minute = clock; served/rep rose.
v21 left aisle at 142 with queue empty and a free till: at till 1 from 142; script found no minute with a free till and a non-empty queue.
No queued wait ever reached patience in ~2400 checked minutes, but no visitor ever walked out in any run (queue at most 2), so the leaving rule (goods back, rep -2, walked_out +1) was never seen.
Visitors on the aisle at clock 479 were gone at 480 (screen evening) with passed, walked_out and served unchanged.
With Second till: tills has 2 entries, 5 minutes with both busy; never till 2 taking while till 1 was free.
With Sign, regular v3 with empty basket took bread from back (1,1) and others took back-row apples at col 0 (front empty); the no-Sign check flags these, the Sign check passes.
Taken order with 6 apples in stock: 'Order delivered: 36', coins +36, apples gone; with no apples: 'Order failed', rep 69->64; untaken order: no line, no change.
Bread bought day 1 morning: 'Bread: sold 0, spoiled 6' that evening; fish bought day 1 spoiled 6 day 2 evening (seed 2); honey days_left stays null.
Seed 3 day 2 heat: apples bought that day went 5->3 without Cool box, 5->4 with it.
Rent 24 (Normal, 2 crates), 15 Easy no crates, 19 Easy 2 crates, Alquiler: 30 Hard no crates; taken from coins.

Evening texts Evening, Day N of 7, Taken/Served/Walked out/Passed matching state, per-good sold/spoiled/left lines matching sales and stock, Rent, Coins, Reputation, Tomorrow: Heat equals forecast[1].
Enter on Evening: Upgrades, Coins: 50, Next day, Second till: 80, Cool box: 40, Sign: 30, Extra crates: 50, Awning: 35; Enter on Next day -> Morning Day 2 of 7.
Cool box 83->43, 'Cool box: owned', Enter again no change; Second till with 10 coins: nothing, 'No hay monedas suficientes' shown; Extra crates: crate_limit 12, 'Crates: 8 of 12'.
Seed 2 Easy day 2 coins -6: Evening 'Bankrupt', slots all null, Enter -> Bankrupt, Score: 0, Days: 2; records [{score 0, bankrupt true}].
Easy 3-day season: Season over, Score: 65 (15+50), Days: 3, Best: 65; slot emptied; title then had no Continue.
After 7 ended seasons: 5 records, 65 first then four score-0 in order ended; lines 'Score 65, 3 days, Easy', 'Score 0, 1 days, Normal, bankrupt'; a later run showed them too.
'Stamp: First coin','Stamp: Sold out' day 1; later evenings only the new one (Full stall, Good name); stamps in stamp order; later run's Stamps screen 'First coin: yes'... 'Rain trade: no'.
First coin on a day with payments (not on a no-sale day); Full stall on a day opened with 8 crates; Whole season on 3-day Easy season ended with 15 coins.
Sold out earned when crated apples/bread went to 0; not earned when fish without a crate went to 0 (seed 2, stamps stayed []).
Day 2 after Continue (with --seed 7) and the same day in one unbroken run: identical md5 of visitors, sales, coins, stock, evening texts.
Repeated runs with same seed and fresh copies gave identical outputs (md5); seeds 1-7 gave different forecasts and wholesale prices.
Run with left on title, put and finish on Morning, accept and rush on Stall, escape on Evening had the same md5 as with none.
modules/work/data goods.json, visitors.json, rates.json (hours 10..8, weather 100/90/50/80/70), upgrades.json, stamps.json; README says how to change each.
Stall frame: two rows of six cell places, five crates in different colours at their cells, cursor outline on (2,0), text Good: Honey, Price: 9, Crates: 5 of 8.

Day frame: stall crates, aisle row with two tourists and a regular at x 0,1,3 in distinct colours, till box, texts 09:33, Speed, Coins, Taken, Served, Reputation. The queue was empty in the frame taken.
Settings and Upgrades frames show their texts with '>' on the chosen row; other screens' frames use the same text column (texts verified per screen in state).
README has how to play, where kept (--settings folder, keys), and the play / frame commands, which worked as written.

defects: Records line says '1 days' for a one-day season.
Each headless run prints on stderr: 'a screen shows {work.shown}: nothing keeps work.shown' (the first frame before the state is set).
Quit given at tick 8 ends the run with tick 9 printed, one tick after the word.
could_not_check: d14: the 99-unit stock cap needs over 96 units of one good, which I never reached in play (the code has STOCK_CAP 99)
d37: no visitor ever walked out in about 2,400 simulated minutes over 6 days (queue at most 2), so I never saw the walk-out effects

builder.note: The builder stopped every examen process by name (taskkill /F /IM examen.exe) and with them the harness watching it; the builder itself ran to its own end, and its cost is recorded by hand from its stream (output tokens from the stream's two result lines).

where.how: weighted_by_kind is exact (the run's own token counts times the weights); a step's kind is a reading of its command's text, and answered_tokens / written_tokens are characters / 4

trace.how: context, new, read_again and how far the context grew are the run's own records. written_out a request is its growth less its answers (characters / 4), scaled to the run's exact total; of_which_unseen is that less the visible text (thinking). cost is what the request read and wrote, weighted; carried is what reading again what it added cost at every later request (start.carried: the same for what every request starts from). reading + writing is in_the_ledger
